cse-2005-cs-85b.approach: Concept tested: **normalising with a hidden bit**. Shift the mantissa $0.00111101$ left until its first 1 is just before the point (3 places), lower the exponent by 3, and store only the bits after that 1 (padding with 0s, as the question says).

steps.title: Find the first 1
steps.body: From part (a), $0.239 \times 2^{13} \approx 0.00111101_2 \times 2^{13}$. The first 1 is in the 3rd place after the point.

steps.title: Shift left by 3
steps.body: $0.00111101 \times 2^{13} = 1.11101 \times 2^{10}$: the significand is multiplied by $2^3$, so the exponent drops from 13 to 10.

steps.title: Fields
steps.body:
- Exponent: $10 + 64 = 74 = 100\,1010_2$.
- Mantissa: the 1 before the point is implicit, so store the bits after it, $11101$, padded with 0s to 8 bits: $1110\,1000$. (These are exactly the 8 bits of part (a) shifted left by 3.)

optionAnalysis.reason: `0A 20`: exponent stored without the bias of 64, and the mantissa byte is wrong.
`11 34`: exponent field $0010001 = 17$, i.e. $E = -47$, unrelated to the number.
`49 D0`: exponent 73 (shift of 4) with mantissa $11010000$, which drops one of the 1s: it encodes $1.1101 \times 2^9 = 928$, not 1952.

cse-2005-cs-85b.shortcut: Normalising never changes the value, so decode the options: (D) gives $1.11101_2 \times 2^{10} = 1.90625 \times 1024 = 1952$, the same as part (a)'s $61/256 \times 2^{13} = 1952$.
pitfalls: Writing $1.1101 \times 2^{10}$ (one 1 lost while shifting): $0.00111101$ has five 1s, so $1.11101$ keeps five 1s.
Shifting left but *raising* the exponent.
Storing the leading 1 as well (`4A F4`), which a hidden-bit format never does.
cse-2005-cs-85b.verification: Part (a) stores $61/256 \times 2^{13} = 1952$. Option (D) stores $(1 + 29/32) \times 2^{10} = 1952$. Same value, so no bits were lost and the key D is fully consistent (an older review note claiming the question was flawed miscounted the 1s).
